Who tracks the sector: free government procurement databases are the primary record, with dedicated defense-intelligence firms layered on top - this page starts with the sources anyone can verify.

analysis.body:
Defense is one of the most active sectors for AI adoption, but measured adoption figures from standard surveys do not cover it in the way they cover commercial industries, so the picture here is assembled from procurement records, program offices, and specialist analysts rather than a single headline rate. The primary public window into what the Department of Defense is actually buying sits in three interconnected federal systems: SAM.gov, which serves as the government's official record for contract opportunities, awards, and vendor registrations and is free and searchable; USAspending.gov, which publishes every federal award and is built on the underlying Federal Procurement Data System feed; and FPDS itself, which records DoD contract actions and vendor performance history at the transaction level, though its standalone search tool has been retired and users are now directed to SAM.gov for that functionality.

The Defense Innovation Unit is the principal commercial on-ramp for AI entering formal DoD programs, with its stated mission being to convert entrepreneurial products into tangible combat power. DIU maintains public project listings, making it the most transparent single source for understanding which commercial AI capabilities are being piloted or transitioned into programs of record. The areas the sourced material points toward most directly are decision support, autonomy, and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance processing, reflecting where DoD acquisition offices have concentrated solicitation activity.

Govini operates as a defense-intelligence platform used inside the Department, tracking procurement trends, supply-chain risk, and vendor capability in AI and autonomy, and it publishes public scorecards on critical-technology spending. The platform it describes transforms activated data into adaptive workflows, mobilized agents, and AI-driven orchestration that proactively forecasts issues, prioritizes recommendations, and aligns resources, which captures the kind of applied decision-science layer that sits between raw procurement data and operational insight.

Janes provides what it describes as validated, peer-reviewed defence intelligence, applying imagery analysis, advanced modeling, and a large global dataset to help analysts move from fragmented reporting to a connected view of capability, intent, and risk. It explicitly positions its data as foundational for the Joint Intelligence Preparation of the Operational Environment process, which places it squarely in the AI-assisted analysis workflow that defense organizations are building. Silicon Valley Defense Group, a nonprofit, monitors the intersection of commercial technology, private capital, and national security, publicly mapping the companies driving AI adoption in the DoD space, though the page harvested at the time of this review did not return substantive content from that organization.

For a buyer or policymaker deciding whether and how to engage, the practical starting point is the public procurement infrastructure. SAM.gov and USAspending.gov together make it possible to trace AI-related solicitations and awards at the transaction level without a subscription, and DIU's public listings show which commercial capabilities have already cleared an initial government vetting. The regulatory environment is shaped by federal acquisition rules, Controlled Unclassified Information handling requirements under 32 CFR Part 2002, and the GSA's ongoing consolidation of procurement systems, all of which add compliance overhead that commercial-only vendors entering this space should account for. The sources are largely silent on specific contract values, ROI findings, or adoption percentages, so claims circulating elsewhere about defense AI spending should be checked directly against USAspending and SAM.gov data before being relied upon.
